title: Labour, Migration & Humanitarian Bodies — ILO, IOM, UNHCR, UNICEF, UNDP, WFP, FAO
shortDescription: Seven bodies that look similar on the surface — agency vs programme vs fund status is the actual thing being tested here.
genZNote: Same UN family, seven different job descriptions — refugees, children, food, hunger, work, migration, development.

sections.heading: ILO — International Labour Organization
bullets: Established: 1919, under the Treaty of Versailles — making it the OLDEST body in this list, predating the UN itself (it later became the UN's first specialized agency, in 1946).
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland.
A UN specialized agency (not a programme/fund) — unique for its 'tripartite' structure: governments, employers, and workers' representatives all sit at the table.
Sets international labour standards through Conventions and Recommendations; won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.

sections.heading: IOM — International Organization for Migration
bullets: Established: 1951; became a 'related organization' of the UN system in 2016 (it operated independently for decades before formally joining the UN family).
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland.
The leading intergovernmental body working on migration — assists migrants, displaced persons, and governments on migration policy and humanitarian response.

sections.heading: UNHCR — UN High Commissioner for Refugees
bullets: Established: 1950, by UN General Assembly resolution — a UN PROGRAMME, not a specialized agency.
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland.
Mandate: protect refugees, forcibly displaced people, and stateless persons, and help find lasting solutions (resettlement, return, local integration).
Won the Nobel Peace Prize twice (1954 and 1981).

sections.heading: UNICEF — UN Children's Fund
bullets: Established: 1946 (originally for post-WWII emergency relief for children in Europe; mandate broadened in 1953 to all children worldwide).
Headquarters: New York, USA.
A UN FUND (created by GA resolution, funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions) — works on child health, nutrition, education, and protection worldwide.

sections.heading: UNDP — UN Development Programme
bullets: Established: 1965, headquartered in New York.
A UN PROGRAMME — the UN's global development network, coordinating on poverty reduction, governance, and (notably) publishing the annual Human Development Report and Human Development Index (HDI).

sections.heading: WFP — World Food Programme
bullets: Established: 1961, headquartered in Rome, Italy.
A UN PROGRAMME — the world's largest humanitarian organization addressing hunger, delivering food assistance in emergencies and working on long-term food security.
Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.

sections.heading: FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization
bullets: Established: 1945, headquartered in Rome, Italy.
A UN specialized agency — leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve agriculture, forestry, and fisheries globally.
Publishes the widely-cited 'State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World' report; distinct from WFP, which does the on-the-ground food DELIVERY.

sections.heading: Agency vs Programme vs Fund — At a Glance

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: ILO and FAO are UN specialized agencies; UNHCR, UNICEF, UNDP and WFP are UN programmes/funds created by GA resolution; IOM is a UN-related organization — same UN family, four different legal statuses.
keyFacts: ILO (1919) is the oldest body here, older than the UN itself; tripartite structure (govt + employers + workers).
FAO and WFP are both Rome-headquartered but do different jobs: FAO = policy/research, WFP = on-ground food delivery.
UNHCR (refugees) est. 1950; UNICEF (children) est. 1946; UNDP (development) est. 1965 — all UN programmes/funds, HQ'd differently.
IOM only formally joined the UN system as a related organization in 2016, despite existing since 1951.
commonConfusion: FAO (agency, policy/research) and WFP (programme, direct food delivery) are both Rome-based and both about food — but their classification and role are different.
IOM existed since 1951 but only became UN-affiliated in 2016 — don't assume its UN membership date equals its founding date.

highYieldFacts: ILO: 1919 (Treaty of Versailles), Geneva — oldest of this group, Nobel Peace Prize 1969.
FAO and WFP both HQ'd in Rome but FAO is a specialized agency while WFP is a programme.
UNDP publishes the Human Development Index (HDI) annually.
commonTraps: Do not call UNICEF or UNHCR a 'specialized agency' — both are UN funds/programmes, a distinct legal category.
Do not assume IOM has been a UN body since its founding — it joined formally only in 2016.
mustRemember: ILO's defining feature: tripartite structure (government + employer + worker representation).
WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020; UNHCR won it in 1954 and 1981; ILO won it in 1969.

confusedTerms.distinction: FAO (specialized agency, 1945) works on agricultural policy, research, and long-term food security; WFP (programme, 1961) physically delivers food assistance during emergencies.

possibleQuestions: Which UN body is the OLDEST — ILO, FAO, UNICEF, or UNDP?
Is UNICEF a UN specialized agency? If not, what is it correctly classified as?
